notes: The unsafe-exposure ratchet is now a real CI gate. .github/workflows/unsafe-exposure-ratchet.sh (invoked from the unsafe-ratchet job in test.yml) runs `cargo geiger --forbid-only --output-format Json` plus `cargo metadata --locked` (the SBOM), then pipes both into the susi-gawd binary `unsafe_ratchet` (src/bin/unsafe_ratchet.rs) — the production caller of ratchet_unsafe. The pinned baseline .agents/baseline/unsafe-default.json records the feature set (default), measured exposure (605 crates: 590 third-party, 15 first-party exceptions incl. justified-FFI susi crates), and the full SBOM (871 entries) — generated locally against the real tree, not seeded. Transitive changes are reported via sbom_changes on every run. The auditable review path: `unsafe-exposure-ratchet.sh <baseline> --write-baseline` regenerates the pinned baseline and committing that diff is the acceptance record; NeedsReview exits 2 and names the crates. Honest limits: the gate measures each crate's unsafe-forbiddance surface (per-crate forbids_unsafe, exposure unit = 1 per non-forbidding crate) rather than per-function unsafe counts — full `cargo geiger` scanning cannot resolve this workspace's vendored path-dependency layout (it hangs in source matching); the parser still accepts full-scan `unsafety.used.functions.unsafe` counts if that ever becomes viable.
